test_title: PYST 05: SSC Stenographer - General Awareness (Held On: 11 Dec 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is the correct explanation of painting and sculpture of Ajanta and Elora caves?

options.text: They are designed in Persian art form
They are representations of medieval Islamic art
They are symbolic representations of Gods in Judaism.
They are depiction of Buddhist religious art.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are**__ __**depiction of Buddhist religious art**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ajanta caves, which date back to the 2nd century BCE to 480 CE, are renowned for their exquisite Buddhist murals and sculptures.
 
• The Ellora caves, constructed between the 6th and 9th centuries, also include significant Buddhist artwork alongside Hindu and Jain art.
 
• These caves were used as monasteries, worship halls, and living quarters for Buddhist monks and are rich in iconography of the Buddha and various Bodhisattvas.
 
• The paintings and sculptures in these caves depict scenes from the life of the Buddha as well as Jataka tales, which are stories of the Buddha's previous lives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• Located in Maharashtra, India, the Ajanta caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The caves were rediscovered in 1819 by a British officer on a hunting expedition.
 
• The artworks are considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, influencing Indian art that followed.
 
 
 
• **Ellora Caves:**
 
 
• Ellora is also located in Maharashtra and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The site includes 34 caves excavated from the basalt cliffs, featuring Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain temples and monasteries.
 
• The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Iconography:**
 
 
• Buddhist art in these caves typically includes depictions of the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and various scenes from Buddhist scriptures.
 
• The use of symbols such as the lotus flower, the wheel, and the Bodhi tree are prevalent in Buddhist art.
 
 
 
• **Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• These are a voluminous body of literature concerning the previous births of Gautama Buddha in both human and animal form.
 
• The tales are intended to convey moral lessons and are often depicted in the artwork of the Ajanta caves.
